contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-payment-sheet-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-payment-sheet-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-payment-sheet.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-sheet`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-sheet, both the April 22 capture (old raw lines 4-39 and 41-92) and the November 7 capture (new raw lines 5-52 and 54-109) describe Stripe’s recommended prebuilt, customizable Payment Sheet for most iOS, Android and React Native apps. The in-app UI provides automatic, vertical or horizontal layout, Appearance API styling, localized forms, dynamic method display/order and A/B testing, Dashboard or Custom Payment Methods, and possible Apple Pay and Link express buttons. Access to over 100 methods is catalog access. Both document saving cards, US bank and SEPA debit, automatic UI consent collection and card-brand filtering. Both dated captures use ‘saved payment method’ for optional CVC recollection (old raw line 91 and new raw line 108). The verified implementation concerns a saved card: the April 22, 2026 Mobile Payment Element deferred server-confirmation route collects details before creating a PaymentIntent and uses the card-specific require_cvc_recollection option (raw/stripe-inapp-finalize-payments-server-2025.md lines 774-791, 808-819 and 2875-2894). That supports the mapped source’s saved-card scope at line 55 without extending the capability to US bank or SEPA debit. CustomerSessions API controls the save checkbox, saved-list visibility and method removal, including protecting the last method. When a Stripe customer identity is supplied, native Payment Sheet supports Customer objects and excludes customer-configured Accounts (new raw lines 9-13). The capture does not require a Customer or CustomerSession for every payment. The retained iOS StripePaymentSheet 26.11.0 snapshot declares optional customer configuration (StripePaymentSheet.podspec line 6 and PaymentSheetConfiguration.swift lines 129-131). The retained React Native 0.84.0 snapshot makes customerId optional and includes a SetupParamsBase branch without a CustomerSession secret or ephemeral key (package.json line 3 and src/types/PaymentSheet.ts lines 19-26 and 115-132). These are versioned SDK declarations, separate from April’s customer-bound save-for-reuse flow and from production payment outcomes. Customer identity and CustomerSession access are distinct from PaymentIntent payment or SetupIntent without an initial charge. The US Android digital-goods note allows in-app Payment Sheet and points iOS to app-to-web Checkout. Tap to Add is a separate access-request private preview, explicitly Android-only with compatible NFC hardware in its dedicated November guide. Both captures allow configurable billing name, email, phone and address; November adds supported-country full-address autocomplete with no additional setup and Google Maps policy conditions. source-stripe-inapp-payment-sheet.md captures most of April’s stable behavior and uses a separately supported appearance count. It omits November’s identity, preview and autocomplete boundaries and compresses saved-method controls. Its saved-card CVC scope has the dated implementation support above.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/payment-sheet, compare old raw lines 8-39 and 64-92 with new raw lines 9-52 and 77-109 when updating source-stripe-inapp-payment-sheet.md. Substantive November clarifications are native Payment Sheet’s Customer-only identity compatibility when an identity is supplied, disclosure of the access-request Tap to Add private preview, and Stripe autocomplete for full billing addresses in supported countries with no extra setup. Google Maps Platform Acceptable Use Policy applies, with possible disablement or other action. Carry reciprocal route warnings for the ambiguous “This feature is available across all supported platforms” and the contemporaneous dedicated guide’s explicit Android-only compatible-NFC-device private preview, and for that native Payment Sheet identity boundary versus the dated Embedded Payment Element Account-or-Customer server route and general Accounts v2 or hosted Checkout guidance. Keep the separately scoped 100+ Payment Sheet catalog and 40+ mobile dynamic display counts and the automatic consent UI alongside merchant compliance obligations. Date April’s US Android/iOS app-to-web note, demo and legacy links, and preserve its raw provenance. App Clip versus download QR is demo navigation, the address link changes from an iOS payment-element route to payment-sheet, the saved-method link drops the iOS qualifier and setup moves to accept-payment type=setup. CDN assets, wording and generic layout labels establish neither an SDK version change nor deprecated integrations. The retained iOS and React Native SDK declarations support optional customer configuration within their snapshot scope. Neither a Customer nor a CustomerSession is required for every payment. Preserve the April and November ‘saved payment method’ CVC wording alongside the dated saved-card server-confirmation implementation. Keep Customer, CustomerSession, PaymentIntent and SetupIntent separate, and scope integration version/secret/event details to linked implementation authority. Method visibility, customer consent, setup and a UI result cannot establish completed payment or settlement.
